question: A 52-year-old Caucasian male presents to your office with an 8 mm dark lesion on his back. The lesion, as seen below, has irregular borders and marked internal color variation. Upon excisional biopsy, the presence of which of the following would best estimate the risk of metastasis in this patient’s lesion:?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Irregular borders and marked internal color variation" -> "suspicion of melanoma" -> "excisional biopsy performed" -> "histopathological examination" -> "identification of cellular atypia" -> "increased risk of metastasis" -> 80% CHAIN: "Excisional biopsy" -> "identification of vertical tumor growth" -> "increased risk of metastasis" -> 75% CHAIN: "Presence of palisading nuclei" -> "suggestive of basal cell carcinoma" -> "lower risk of metastasis" -> 70% CHAIN: "Increased production of melanosomes" -> "suggestive of melanoma" -> "increased risk of metastasis" -> 80%
enhanced_information: In this case, the presence of cellular atypia upon histopathological examination of the lesion would best estimate the risk of metastasis in the patient. Cellular atypia is a key feature associated with increased risk of metastasis in melanoma lesions. The evidence path of (Excision biopsy)-CAUSES->(Symptoms)-CAUSES->(Disease)-CAUSES->(Histopathology) supports the importance of histopathological examination in evaluating the lesion.
analysis: The core medical principle in assessing the risk of metastasis in melanoma lesions is based on histopathological features. Cellular atypia is a key feature associated with increased risk of metastasis in melanoma. While other features like palisading nuclei, keratin pearls, vertical tumor growth, and increased production of melanosomes are important in diagnosing melanoma, cellular atypia is specifically linked to a higher risk of metastasis.
